cells.quote: DxJ [+ 0.29(0.02)] and cognitive errors [– 0.42(0.03)] showed the strongest associations with diagnostic accuracy; test ordering [+ 0.18(0.01)] and building a Ddx [+ 0.12(0.01)] also had significant, though smaller, effects
cells.note: Because cognitive errors have a negative coefficient for correct diagnosis, fewer errors are associated with better diagnostic accuracy. The estimate is an unstandardized GEE logistic-regression coefficient.

D.treatment: later cases after repeated deliberate practice and feedback

cells.quote: Cognitive errors dropped by half from 0.87 to 0.43 per student per case, and misdiagnoses fell threefold from 27% to 9.0% (Fig. 3, p < 0.0001).
cells.note: The learning-curve analysis is longitudinal and observational; no random assignment to practice amount was reported.

O.outcome_detail: diagnostic reasoning, investigation ordering, misdiagnosis, and cognitive-error performance

cells.quote: By the end of pre-clerkship, the M1 cohort outperformed the M2 cohort at the end of pre-clerkship for all of: performing DxJ, ordering investigations, misdiagnosis rates, and rates of cognitive errors (Fig. 4, p < 0.0001).
cells.note: The cohorts were not randomly assigned and differed in year and exposure to the curriculum; lower misdiagnosis and cognitive-error rates are better.
